newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Two Swedish air force jets collide in mid-air.
newsitem.headline: Two Swedish air force jets collide in mid-air.

text.p: Two Swedish air force jets on Thursday collided in mid-air five km (three miles) east of the central Swedish town of Ramsele, the Swedish defence ministry said in a statement.
It said both pilots had bailed out and were still alive, but their condition was unknown.
The two JA 37 Viggen jets from the F4 Air Force squadron based in Ostersund collided at 0740 GMT while they were taking part in a routine exercise, a spokeswoman from the ministry said.
"The pilots from the other aircraft saw the two men waving at them, so we know they are not dead, but we are not yet sure of their condition," she told Reuters.

Squadron commander Aspbjorn Norling told news agency TT he had no further details of the incident. "We don't know whether it was down to the human factor or a technical fault," he said, adding that rescue teams were on their way to the site.
In August, a Swedish Air Force AJS 37 Viggen crashed into the Baltic Sea while on exercise near Ornskoldsvik, 565 km (350 miles) north of Stockholm. The pilot was killed.
